Class Theme

java.lang.Object
guiTools.Theme
public class Theme extends Object

Title: Theme Class.

Description: One place that decides how every screen other than the Admin screens looks, so that they look like parts of the same application rather than a collection of pages.

The decisions encoded here are the ones recorded in User Experience.pdf after the team compared five professional sign-in pages. Five of them shaped this class:

  • the form sits in one narrow centred column, because that was the only layout every one of the five had in common;
  • every field has a visible label above it rather than grey placeholder text inside it, because placeholder text disappears as soon as the user starts typing and a user who is interrupted comes back to a box with nothing to say what it wanted;
  • there is exactly one filled button on a screen, so the next action is never in doubt; everything else is drawn quietly;
  • supporting and secondary actions are smaller and set below the main one, out of the way of the main task;
  • nothing relies on colour alone, so the screens still read for somebody who cannot tell red from green.

The Admin screens are deliberately left as they were supplied, which the assignment permits, so nothing in this class is applied to them.

This class only sets fonts, colours, sizes and positions. It does not create widgets, take decisions about behaviour, or perform validation, so restyling a screen cannot change what that screen does.
